pieces.name: Cat's Eye
pieces.spec: n = 2.0 ball · silvered back · returns light

levels.name: First Light
levels.tip: Drag the mirror onto the bench, then click it to turn it. Bounce the beam into the photocell.

levels.name: Dogleg
levels.tip: Three mirrors. Go under the wall, then come back up.

levels.name: Pinhole
levels.tip: A pinhole cell only catches the middle of a wide beam. A convex lens squeezes all five rays to a point.

levels.name: Corner Pocket
levels.tip: A concave mirror turns the beam and focuses it in one move. Only its silvered front reflects.

levels.name: Sidestep
levels.tip: A tilted glass block bends the beam in and back out, shifting it sideways without changing its direction.

levels.name: Floodlight
levels.tip: Three cells, one beam. A concave lens fans the rays apart.

levels.name: Fork
levels.tip: The blue see-through plate is a beam splitter, not a mirror: half the light passes straight through, half bounces off. Use the mirror to steer the bounced half.

levels.name: Spectrum
levels.tip: A prism splits white light into its colours. Each coloured cell only counts its own wavelength.

levels.name: Scatter Shot
levels.tip: A convex mirror reflects and spreads at the same time.

levels.name: Periscope
levels.tip: Climb the wall, then focus.

levels.name: Two Colours
levels.tip: Red bends least, green bends more. Aim the rainbow, then steer it.

levels.name: Crossed Wires
levels.tip: Beams pass through each other. Get red to red and blue to blue.

levels.name: Half and Half
levels.tip: One white beam, a white cell and a blue cell.

levels.name: Grand Bench
levels.tip: Everything you have learned. Split it twice, focus one branch, colour another.

levels.name: Critical Angle
levels.tip: Light inside glass that meets the flat face at more than 42° cannot get out. It reflects completely. Turn the block until it does.

levels.name: Return to Sender
levels.tip: A cat's eye sends light straight back the way it came, whatever angle it arrives at. Split it on the way out and again on the way back.

levels.name: Light Pipe
levels.tip: Light that enters an optical fiber bounces along inside it, even around corners. Feed the open end.

levels.name: Plumbing
levels.tip: Fiber ends that touch join up. Lay a pipe for the light: up, over the wall, and out.

levels.name: Mirage
levels.tip: Air over the hot plate is thinner, so light skimming across it curves back up. That is the shimmering puddle on a summer road.

levels.name: Raindrop
levels.tip: Light enters a raindrop, reflects off the back and comes out split into colours, heading back toward the light. Every rainbow is made this way.

levels.name: Fire
levels.tip: A diamond's facets trap light and throw it back out as flashes of colour. Jewellers call it fire.

levels.name: Grand Lab
levels.tip: Everything from this lab. Split the beam, send one half home and pipe the other under the wall.

levels.name: Needle of Light
levels.tip: Gather all nine rays into the tiny iris. Slide the convex lens until the bright focus sits inside it. Tap a part, then click a hole to place it.

levels.name: Paint with Light
levels.tip: Light all five strips of the receiver. A narrow bright spot does not count: spread the beam with the concave lens. Each strip needs 10 lm.

levels.name: Twin Focus
levels.tip: Split the light, then focus both branches into their tiny irises. Each needs 45 lm at the same time. A splitter shares energy; it does not create more.

levels.name: Through the Needle
levels.tip: Focus through the slit, then use a second convex lens to make a wide parallel beam again. Fill all five strips with rays arriving within 2 degrees of straight.

levels.name: Switchback
levels.tip: Two barriers, opposite openings. Plan the entire route before spending your six mirrors.

levels.name: The Inner Vault
levels.tip: The receiver sits inside a folded corridor. Work backward from its entrance.

levels.name: Power Budget
levels.tip: Each splitter halves the power. Give the pinhole the first half; share what remains between the other two cells.

levels.name: Chromatic Weave
levels.tip: Three colours, three destinations, one shared bench. Light can cross light; hardware blocks both.

levels.name: Twin Needles
levels.tip: Both branches need nearly all of their half-beam. Route first, then put each focus at its pinhole.

levels.name: Echo Chamber
levels.tip: A returning beam meets the same splitter from the other side. Two journeys can share the same piece.

levels.name: Fiber Exchange
levels.tip: Bridge the gaps between the bolted fibers. Every bend must join its neighbours; aim the source into the open end.

levels.name: Spectrum Lock
levels.tip: Keep one branch white. Send the other around the barrier before separating its red and violet light.

levels.name: Four-Way Contract
levels.tip: Four cells demand different shares: half, quarter, and two eighths. Decide the splitting order before routing the branches.

levels.name: Grandmaster
levels.tip: A pinhole, a white cell and two spectral locks. Save half the power for the focus, then divide the remaining light.
